{{nihongo|'''Ozeki Shrine'''|小塞神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

{{wikidata link|Q11459557|ja|小塞神社|grok=none|check_date=2026-06-06}}

'''Ozeki Shrine''' (おぜきじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Azai|Q11556970|qid=Q11556970|lt=Asai-chō}}, {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|Q270810|qid=Q270810}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was gōsha. It is the origin of the local place name “Ozeki.”

It is presumed to be “Ozeki Shrine” of {{ill|Nakashima district|Q780420|qid=Q780420}}, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}. However, this area is in {{ill|Haguri District|hu|Haguri körzet|ja|葉栗郡|ko|하구리군 (아이치현)|pl|Powiat Haguri|sr|Област Хагури|zh|葉栗郡|qid=Q1032507}} of Owari, so this is questioned. Still, there are similar cases: “Ishitō Shrine,” also a Shikinaisha of Nakajima District, is theorized to be {{ill|Iwato Shrine|ja|石刀神社|qid=Q11585184}}, and {{ill|Azai Shrine (Ichinomiya)|ja|浅井神社 (一宮市)|qid=Q11556984}}, also a Nakajima District Shikinaisha, exists in Haguri District. Since this region frequently flooded by the {{ill|Kiso River|arz|نهر كيسو|bg|Кисо (река)|ceb|Kiso-gawa|cs|Kiso|de|Kiso (Fluss)|es|Río Kiso|eu|Kiso ibaia|fa|رود کیسو|fr|Kiso-gawa|he|קיסו (נהר)|it|Kiso|ja|木曽川|ko|기소강|pl|Kiso|ru|Кисо (река)|tr|Kiso Nehri|uk|Кісо (річка)|zh|木曾川|qid=Q779607}}, another theory says district boundaries in the Heian period were unclear, so this area may also have belonged to Nakajima District.

=== Overview ===
*Foundation period is unknown. The main sanctuary stands on a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|ko|전방후원분|simple|Zenpō-kōen-fun|zh|前方後圓墳|qid=Q11268718}}. This kofun is traditionally said to be the tomb of Ozeki Sukune Yumihari (ancestor of the {{ill|Owari clan|fa|خاندان اوواری|ja|尾張氏|qid=Q11465311}}). The area is a dense zone of small kofun known as the Asai Kofun Group. {{ill|Azai Shrine (Ichinomiya)|ja|浅井神社 (一宮市)|qid=Q11556984|lt=Asai Shrine}} also has its shrine buildings on a kofun.
*In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called Funatsuki Daimyōjin. There was a landing here, and boats for Ise Shrine pilgrimages are said to have come and gone using the Kiso River.
*In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6), it was renamed back to Ozeki Shrine and became a village shrine.
*In {{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}} (Meiji 42), Saigūshi Shrine, Nishi-Shinmei-sha, and Atago-sha were merged.

=== Cultural properties ===
* Ozeki Shrine Kofun - Aichi Prefecture designated historic site, one of the Asai Kofun Group
* Shrine forest - Ichinomiya City designated natural monument

=== Transportation ===
*Get off at {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|ja|名鉄バス|qid=Q6810397}} “Ozeki” stop, 5 minutes on foot
**From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Q2856589|qid=Q2856589}} on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|de|Meitetsu Nagoya-Hauptlinie|fr|Ligne principale Meitetsu Nagoya|it|Linea Meitetsu Nagoya principale|ja|名鉄名古屋本線|ko|메이테쓰 나고야 본선|nl|Meitetsu Nagoya-lijn|pt|Linha Meitetsu Nagoya|su|Jalur Utama Meitetsu Nagoya|zh|名古屋本線|qid=Q1137838}}/{{ill|Meitetsu Bisai Line|Q901005|qid=Q901005}} of {{ill|Meitetsu|Q30850|qid=Q30850}}, or {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Q871495|qid=Q871495}} on the {{ill|Tōkaidō Main Line|Q1190152|qid=Q1190152}} (Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station bus terminal platform 3), take bus bound for “Miyata Hongō”
